nodes.name: Big bluestem
nodes.desc: The dominant tall grass of the Flint Hills prairie, and the main forage for grazing bison and cattle.

nodes.name: Indiangrass
nodes.desc: A tall warm-season grass that grows alongside big bluestem and is grazed by bison.

nodes.name: Little bluestem
nodes.desc: A shorter bunchgrass found on the thin, rocky upland soils of the Flint Hills.

nodes.name: Prairie wildflowers
nodes.desc: Compass plant, gayfeather, milkweed and many other wildflowers add most of the prairie plant diversity and feed insects and browsers.

nodes.name: Eastern red cedar
nodes.desc: A woody tree that spreads into unburned prairie; the Flint Hills are threatened by this woody encroachment.

nodes.name: American bison
nodes.desc: A herd of about 200 bison grazes part of Konza Prairie. Wikipedia notes bison once grazed the region in huge numbers before being nearly wiped out.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Often present in large numbers at Konza. It browses wildflowers and shrubs, and its droppings add nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Eastern cottontail
nodes.desc: A common small grazer of grasses and wildflowers, and prey for many of the prairie predators.

nodes.name: Prairie vole
nodes.desc: A small grass-eating rodent that is well recorded around the park and is a staple prey of hawks and coyotes.

nodes.name: Grasshoppers
nodes.desc: Leaf-eating insects that are abundant in grassland and feed birds, reptiles and small mammals.

nodes.name: Greater prairie-chicken
nodes.desc: Eats seeds and fruit, plus insects such as grasshoppers in summer. The Flint Hills are known for it, and raccoons and other mesopredators take many eggs.

nodes.name: Eastern meadowlark
nodes.desc: A grassland songbird recorded often near the park that eats insects and seeds.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: An omnivore. Wikipedia notes mesopredators such as raccoons raise prairie-chicken egg losses.

nodes.name: Black Rat Snake
nodes.desc: A constrictor that eats rodents, rabbits and birds; GloBI records it feeding on rabbits and cotton rats.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A common raptor hunting voles, rabbits and ground birds over open prairie.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Scavenges carcasses such as deer and rabbits, returning their energy to the web.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: The prairie's main wide-ranging carnivore, eating rabbits, rodents, insects and fawns.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A solitary cat that preys on rabbits, rodents and young deer.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm-season grasses grow fastest in summer sun.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Konza receives roughly 835 mm of rain a year, enough to support woodland if fire and grazing did not hold it back.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Fire keeps trees off the prairie and recycles nutrients; Flint Hills ranchers burn each spring to renew the grass.

nodes.name: Prairie soil
nodes.desc: Deep loess and organic-rich soils hold nutrients; urine and dung from grazers add nitrogen.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
